lado_card.texto: The G1 from MuJoCo Menagerie (62ab00f), the open gait policy from unitree_rl_lab (4960b84), and a ~120-line PPO with the values from mjlab. Tested on 10/19/2026, no GPU.

inicio.kicker: FTH — Humanoid Technology Training · course 1 of 5 · 8 lessons
inicio.titulo: Teaching it to walk: locomotion by RL in simulation
inicio.lead: The Unitree G1 walks because a learned policy sends 29 joint targets every 20 ms. In eight lessons you run a ready-made policy, tune the PD, build the environment, read the reward term by term, train PPO on CPU, read the curves, evaluate with a push, and write your own training plan.
inicio.capa_alt: Graphite-gray industrial humanoid robot with a black visor, mid-step in a dark lab, attached to a steel gantry, with the title Teaching it to walk.

numeros.t: episodes upright with a push (ready-made policy)

inicio.aulas_sub: From the ready-made policy to your training plan: PD on the joints, environment, reward, PPO, curves, evaluation, and terrain curriculum.

itens: People who code in Python, have seen ROS 2 (or took the robot course), and want to understand how a humanoid learns to walk.
People with no humanoid and no GPU: every practice runs on CPU, in minutes, in MuJoCo.
People who took course 0 (the ~/fth bench): this course reuses the venv and the Menagerie.

blocos.t: What you walk away able to do
itens: Run the G1 gait policy in MuJoCo and measure what it does.
Read each term of the gait reward in a recorded rollout and predict the effect of a weight.
Train PPO on CPU, read the curves, and spot reward hacking.
Evaluate with a push and a step, and write a training plan that a script checks.
